arxiv-2110-00059.title: Observational constraints of the modified cosmology through Barrow entropy
arxiv-2110-00059.creator: Mahnaz Asghari, Ahmad Sheykhi
arxiv-2110-00059.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Mahnaz Asghari, Ahmad Sheykhi. Taking into account a fractal structure for the black hole horizon, Barrow argued that the area law of entropy is modified due to quantum-gravitational effects (Barrow in Phys Lett B 808:135643, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.physletb.2020.135643 , 2020). Accordingly, the corrected entropy takes the form S ∼ A 1 + Δ / 2 S\sim A^{1+\mathrm{\Delta}/2} , where 0 ≤ Δ ≤ 1 0\leq\mathrm{\Delta}\leq 1 , indicates the amount of the quantum-gravitational deformation effects.

arxiv-2201-00937.title: Modeling Compact Objects with EFT II: The Post-Newtonian Expansion
arxiv-2201-00937.creator: Irvin Martinez
arxiv-2201-00937.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Irvin Martinez. Part 2 of 3 from the master’s thesis: Modeling Compact Objects with Effective Field Theory. Using the Effective Field Theory framework for extended objects, we build the effective theory of a binary system made up of the most general compact objects in a theory of gravity as General Relativity with electrodynamics, objects which are described by their mass, spin, charge and their finite-size structure.

arxiv-2212-09736.title: Don’t Generate, Discriminate : A Proposal for Grounding Language Models to Real-World Environments
arxiv-2212-09736.creator: Yu Gu, Xiang Deng, Yu Su
arxiv-2212-09736.description: Abstract A key missing capacity of current language models (LMs) is grounding to real-world environments. Most existing work for grounded language understanding uses LMs to directly generate plans that can be executed in the environment to achieve the desired effects. It thereby casts the burden of ensuring grammaticality, faithfulness, and controllability all on the LMs.

arxiv-2308-01589.title: Holy Grail 2.0: From Natural Language to Constraint Models
arxiv-2308-01589.creator: Dimos Tsouros, Hélène Verhaeghe, Serdar Kadıoğlu, Tias Guns
arxiv-2308-01589.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Dimos Tsouros, Hélène Verhaeghe, Serdar Kadıoğlu, Tias Guns. Twenty-seven years ago, E. Freuder highlighted that ”Constraint programming represents one of the closest approaches computer science has yet made to the Holy Grail of programming: the user states the problem, the computer solves it”. Nowadays, CP users have great modeling tools available (like Minizinc and CPMpy), allowing them to formulate the problem and then let a solver do the rest of the job, getting closer to the stated goal.

arxiv-2311-10394.title: Normal Forms and Tyurin Degenerations of K3 Surfaces Polarised by a Rank 18 Lattice Thanks: Charles F. Doran (Alberta/Bard College/CMSA Harvard) was supported by the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC) Thanks: Joseph Prebble (Loughborough) was partially supported by a
arxiv-2311-10394.creator: Charles F. Doran, Joseph Prebble, Alan Thompson
arxiv-2311-10394.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Charles F. Doran, Joseph Prebble, Alan Thompson. We study projective Type II degenerations of K3 surfaces polarised by a certain rank 18 lattice, where the central fibre consists of a pair of rational surfaces glued along a smooth elliptic curve. Given such a degeneration, one may construct other degenerations of the same kind by flopping curves on the central fibre, but the degenerations obtained from this process are not usually projective.

arxiv-2311-16402.title: A unified description of DGLAP, CSS, and BFKL: TMD factorization bridging large and small x
arxiv-2311-16402.creator: Swagato Mukherjee, Vladimir V. Skokov, Andrey Tarasov, Shaswat Tiwari
arxiv-2311-16402.description: Abstract This paper introduces a transverse-momentum dependent (TMD) factorization scheme designed to unify both large and small Bjorken-x regimes. We compute the next-to-leading order (NLO) quantum chromodynamics (QCD) corrections to the gluon TMD operator for an unpolarized hadron within this proposed scheme. This leads to the emergence of a new TMD evolution, incorporating those in transverse momentum, rapidity, and Bjorken-x.

arxiv-2312-15017.title: Interference of resonances in two-proton emission of 16 Ne
arxiv-2312-15017.creator: Tomohiro Oishi, Masaaki Kimura
arxiv-2312-15017.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tomohiro Oishi, Masaaki Kimura. We investigate the two-proton ( 2 ​ p 2p ) emission from 16 Ne with the time-dependent 14 O + p + p +p+p three-body calculations. Two 0 + 0^{+} resonances are suggested to participate. For the 0 1 + 0^{+}_{1} resonance, the true emission of the spatially localized two protons is dominant, if the single-particle s 1 / 2 s_{1/2} resonance locates above the 2 ​ p 2p energy.

arxiv-2403-16017.title: Generalized Kramers-Wanier Duality from Bilinear Phase Map
arxiv-2403-16017.creator: Han Yan (闫寒), Linhao Li
arxiv-2403-16017.description: Abstract We present the Bilinear Phase Map (BPM), a concept that extends the Kramers-Wannier (KW) transformation to investigate unconventional gapped phases, their dualities, and phase transitions. Defined by a matrix of ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} elements, the BPM not only encapsulates the essence of KW duality but also enables exploration of a broader spectrum of generalized quantum phases and dualities.

arxiv-2404-06077.title: Is Your A I Truly Yours? Leveraging B lockcha i n for Copyright s , Provenance, and Lineage
arxiv-2404-06077.creator: Yilin Sai 1,2 , Qin Wang 1,2 , Guangsheng Yu 1 , H.M.N. Dilum Bandara 1,2 , Shiping Chen 1,2
arxiv-2404-06077.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yilin Sai 1,2 , Qin Wang 1,2 , Guangsheng Yu 1 , H.M.N. Dilum Bandara 1,2 , Shiping Chen 1,2. As Artificial Intelligence (AI) integrates into diverse areas, particularly in content generation, ensuring rightful ownership and ethical use becomes paramount. AI service providers are expected to prioritize responsibly sourcing training data and obtaining licenses from data owners.

arxiv-2409-18927.title: Elliptic-elliptic surfaces and the Hesse pencil
arxiv-2409-18927.creator: François Greer and Yilong Zhang
arxiv-2409-18927.description: Abstract . We construct a family of elliptic surfaces with p g = q = 1 p_{g}=q=1 that arise from base change of the Hesse pencil. We identify explicitly a component of the higher Noether-Lefschetz locus with positive Mordell-Weil rank, and a particular surface having maximal Picard number and defined over ℚ \mathbb{Q} .

arxiv-2506-12109.title: Personalized LLM Decoding via Contrasting Personal Preference
arxiv-2506-12109.creator: Hyungjune Bu, Chanjoo Jung, Minjae Kang, Jaehyung Kim
arxiv-2506-12109.description: Abstract As large language models (LLMs) are progressively deployed in various real-world applications, personalization of LLMs has become increasingly important. While various approaches to LLM personalization such as prompt-based and training-based methods have been actively explored, the development of effective decoding-time algorithms remains largely overlooked, despite their demonstrated potential.

arxiv-2509-02965.title: L 2 L^{2} -contraction and asymptotic stability of large shock for scalar viscous conservation laws
arxiv-2509-02965.creator: Alexis F. Vasseur, Yi Wang, Jian Zhang
arxiv-2509-02965.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Alexis F. Vasseur, Yi Wang, Jian Zhang. Abstract : We investigate L^{2} -contraction and time-asymptotic stability of large shock for scalar viscous conservation laws with polynomial flux. For the strictly convex flux f(u)=u^{p} with 2\leq p\leq 4 , we can prove L^{2} -contraction and time-asymptotic stability of arbitrarily large viscous shock profile in H^{1} -framework by using a -contraction method with time-dependent shift and suitable weight function.

arxiv-2511-17458.title: Laminar and Turbulent Flow in Wavy Pipes under Strong Wall Modulations
arxiv-2511-17458.creator: I. El Mellas \aff 1, J. J. Hidalgo \aff 1 and M. Dentz \aff 1
arxiv-2511-17458.description: Abstract We investigate laminar and turbulent flow in pipes with periodically varying cross-sections, using direct numerical simulations over a range of Reynolds numbers between 1 − 5300 1-5300 . Pipe diameters are sinusoidally modulated in the axial direction, resulting in constrictions that reduce the local pipe radius by up to 40 percent.

arxiv-2511-19207.title: Inclinations and Position Angles for Disc Galaxies in the SGA sample
arxiv-2511-19207.creator: Megan H. Martinez ​ 1 , 2 {}^{\lx@orcidlink{0009-0003-5203-8051}{\orcidlogo}{1,2}}, Michael S. Petersen ​ 2 {}^{\lx@orcidlink{0000-0003-1517-3935}{\orcidlogo}{2}}, Carrie Filion ​ 3 {}^{\lx@orcidlink{0000-0001-5522-5029}{\orcidlogo}3}, Rashid Yaaqib ​ 2 , 4 {}^{\lx@orcidlink{0009-0003-9063-1382}{\or
arxiv-2511-19207.description: Abstract We present a data-driven method for determining the inclination and position angle (PA) of disc galaxies using a Fourier-Laguerre basis decomposition of imaging data. We define a dimensionless metric, η \eta , that characterises the ratio of the quadrupole and monopole coefficients in the Fourier-Laguerre basis function expansion.

arxiv-2512-22057.title: Unified Royer Law Revision for α \alpha -Decay Half-Lives: Shell Corrections, Pairing, and Orbital-Angular-Momentum
arxiv-2512-22057.creator: Kai Ren, Pengfei Ma, Minghui Hu, Junlong Tian
arxiv-2512-22057.description: Abstract The Royer law is a widely used empirical relation for calculating α \alpha -decay half-lives but requires 12 parity-dependent parameters. It exhibits systematic deviations near the N = 126 N=126 shell closure. We propose an improved Royer law by adding a shell-correction term, an odd-even pairing indicator, and an orbital-angular-momentum contribution.

arxiv-2602-08620.title: Improving Reconstruction of Representation Autoencoder
arxiv-2602-08620.creator: Siyu Liu, Chujie Qin, Hubery Yin, Qixin Yan, Zheng-Peng Duan, Chen Li, Jing Lyu, Chun-Le Guo, Chongyi Li
arxiv-2602-08620.description: Abstract Recent work leverages Vision Foundation Models as image encoders to boost the generative performance of latent diffusion models (LDMs), as their semantic feature distributions are easy to learn. However, such semantic features often lack low-level information ( e.g . , color and texture), leading to degraded reconstruction fidelity, which has emerged as a primary bottleneck in further scaling LDMs.

pmc-10698490.title: Fundamental bound on epidemic overshoot in the SIR model
pmc-10698490.creator: Maximilian M Nguyen, Ari S Freedman, Sinan A Ozbay, Simon A Levin
pmc-10698490.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). We derive an exact upper bound on the epidemic overshoot for the Kermack–McKendrick SIR model. This maximal overshoot value of 0.2984 · · · occurs at R0∗=2.151⋯. In considering the utility of the notion of overshoot, a rudimentary analysis of data from the first wave of the COVID-19 pandemic in Manaus, Brazil highlights the public health hazard posed by overshoot for epidemics with R0 near 2.

pmc-10735463.title: THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN MEDICAL MARIJUANA USE AND DIVIDED ATTENTION ON A SIMULATED DRIVING PERFORMANCE TASK
pmc-10735463.creator: Nicole Ennis, Daniel Dunleavy, Katie Kloss, Nichole Stetten, Sherrilene Classen
pmc-10735463.description: Driving is a complex and dynamic task requiring divided attention (DA), awareness of the traffic and surroundings while focusing on critical stimulus. The goal of this project was to examine the relationship between medical marijuana use and divided attention in adults 50 and older during a simulated driving performance task.

pmc-12385413.title: The Health Effects of Heated Tobacco Product Use—A Narrative Review
pmc-12385413.creator: Małgorzata Znyk, Dorota Kaleta
pmc-12385413.description: One of the most popular currently available tobacco products is the heated tobacco product (HTP), which heats nicotine and other chemical substances into a vapor for inhalation. The aim of the present review was to clarify the effects of exposure to HTP, which currently remain unclear. A literature search of Web of Science, Scopus, ClinicalKey, and PubMed was conducted.

pmc-12649146.title: Supplementing 25-Hydroxy-Vitamin D3 to Sows Enhances Milk and Blood Parameters, with Extended Benefits to Their Offspring
pmc-12649146.creator: Shanmugam Sureshkumar, Md Raihanul Hoque, In Ho Kim
pmc-12649146.description: Simple SummaryVitamin D is essential for maintaining bone strength, reproductive efficiency, and immune function. In sow diets, it supports healthy pregnancies, optimal milk production, and robust piglet growth. However, research on the use of 25-hydroxy-vitamin D3 (25OHD3), a more biologically active and efficient form of vitamin D in sow nutrition, remains limited.

pmc-13292280.title: Synovial histopathology in rheumatoid arthritis treated with biological disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs: an analysis of 1593 surgical specimens using the Rooney score
pmc-13292280.creator: Masanori Sudo, Asami Abe, Hajime Ishikawa, Sayuri Takamura, Daisuke Kobayashi, Kiyoshi Nakazono, Akira Murasawa, Suguru Yamamoto, Satoshi Ito
pmc-13292280.description: ObjectivesThis study aims to evaluate synovial histopathological inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) using the Rooney score (RS) and to investigate histopathological heterogeneity within difficult-to-treat (D2T) RA.MethodsWe analysed 1593 synovial specimens from 1043 patients with RA who underwent joint surgery between 2013 and 2023. Histological inflammation was assessed by a blinded pathologist using a modified RS (total score, 0-60).

pmc-13300679.title: Cardiac SABR vs. catheter ablation for VT in high-risk IHD patients: early experience from a UK centre
pmc-13300679.creator: D Hunnybun, J Lee, N Kelland, A Kyriacou, G Kirkwood, M A Sammut, P Metherhall, S Riley, M Hatton, S Jamil-Copley
pmc-13300679.description: BackgroundCatheter ablation (CA) is a common management strategy for drug-refractory ventricular tachycardia (VT) in patients with ischaemic heart disease (IHD). Patients that fail CA, currently have limited long-term management options. Cardiac stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (cSABR) is an emerging alternative treatment which is gaining interest worldwide.

pmc-13462201.title: A narrative review of clinical research on knee osteoarthritis in 2025
pmc-13462201.creator: Jie Lv, Chunqing Hu, Hanwen Zhang, Tianle Ou, Dongquan Shi, Zhongyang Lv
pmc-13462201.description: Background and ObjectiveKnee osteoarthritis (KOA) is the most common degenerative joint disease, causing significant social and economic burden globally. KOA management typically follows stepped-care approaches, including lifestyle changes, pharmacological treatments, and surgery. Driven by recent translational breakthroughs in KOA research, clinical management paradigms are increasingly characterized by high degrees of personalization and diagnostic precision.

pmc-13482575.description: Proteostasis collapse, a hallmark of aging and neurodegeneration like Alzheimer’s disease (AD), causes irreversible damage in late life. Whether late-life proteostasis capacity is developmentally programmed remains unclear, as mechanistic studies requiring lifelong tracking and molecular manipulation are challenging or impossible in long-lived species. Using C.

pmc-13585223.title: Character level attention siamese networks for Chinese handwriting comparison
pmc-13585223.creator: Li Zhu, Long Tang, Huaqing Mao, Dhamyaa Abbas Nasrawi, Dhamyaa Abbas Nasrawi, Dhamyaa Abbas Nasrawi
pmc-13585223.description: Handwriting recognition comparison is a critical yet challenging task in financial, commercial, and exam cheating prevention applications. However, the drawbacks of existing methods are that they compare the whole sentence or the entire signature with multiple characters susceptible to data noise. Their accuracy fluctuates widely.

pmc-13679535.title: Effect of Alveolar Ridge Inclination on Dynamic Navigation Accuracy of Implant Surgery: A Retrospective Clinical Study
pmc-13679535.creator: Xuechun Jiang, Ran Zhang, Huiyun Jiang, Ni Zeng, Huimin Nie, Wenjuan Zhou, Zhonghao Liu
pmc-13679535.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo evaluate the accuracy of dynamic navigation-guided dental implantation system across different alveolar ridge inclinations.Materials and MethodsThis retrospective study included 34 patients (120 implants) who underwent dynamic navigation-assisted dental implantation between January 2021 and December 2025. Deviations at the entry point of the initial drill and pilot drill were recorded to analyze the influence of alveolar ridge inclination on surgical accuracy.
